Each sitemap's status (200 or 404) determines whether its associated URL set is fully indexed. The path taxonomy vector encodes semantic categories of content through URL path segments, enabling classification of articles by intent. The frequency tensor captures how often each path segment appears across all URLs, forming a multi-dimensional signal that can be analyzed using tensor methods. These primitives form a dual framework: one for structural indexing (topology), and one for semantic categorization (taxonomy). Failure modes include missing sitemaps leading to unbounded URL counts and sparse tensors causing loss of signal-to-noise ratio. The interplay between these operators allows for robust inference about site architecture and content strategy.
